title: Holi: the festival of colors
hook: Prahlad walks out of the fire unharmed; the next morning everyone throws color and nobody is a stranger

segments.voice: Yesterday, the question about caste, and Satyakama telling the plain truth. Your line was you don't have to defend what you didn't choose. Today, the last day of the stories, and one more fire. Day ninety-six.
screen: `YOU DON'T HAVE TO DEFEND WHAT YOU DIDN'T CHOOSE.`

segments.voice: You've met two Holi stories. Prahlad walking out of the fire. Krishna coloring Radha's face in Braj. Here's a third, and in parts of south India it's the one told at Holi's full moon. Shiva is sitting in meditation on a mountain, so deep and so still that nothing reaches him. He's been there since his first wife, Sati, died. The gods need him to wake up, to marry again, to have a son who can defeat a demon. So they send the god of love, Kama, with his bow of sugarcane and his arrows of flowers, to shoot one into Shiva's heart.
screen: `A THIRD STORY.` → `SHIVA, STILL AS A MOUNTAIN.` → `KAMA DRAWS HIS FLOWER BOW.`

segments.voice: Kama shoots. The arrow lands. And Shiva opens his third eye. Fire pours out of it, and Kama is burned to ash where he stands. His wife, Rati, falls weeping on the ashes. And here the story turns. Shiva, moved, promises that Kama will live again, but without a body. Love, from now on, will be everywhere and visible nowhere. That's why one of Kama's names is Ananga, the bodiless one. And Shiva does wake, and does marry Parvati. In parts of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, Holi's full moon is remembered as Kama Dahanam, the burning of Kama, with fires and songs of Rati's grief. So two of Holi's three stories run through fire. A bonfire that couldn't hold a child. A fire from a god's eye that burns love's body away and sets it loose in the world. And then Krishna and Radha's morning of colors after it. And today is the last day of the stories. For seventy-five days you've met these people. Ganesha and his broken tusk. Rama, Sita and Hanuman. Krishna the butter thief and Krishna the charioteer. The Goddess and her nine nights. The lamps, the colors, the thread. You know them now. Tomorrow the path changes. Camp three is the practices. Less story, more doing: breath, mantra, a home shrine, a day. But the stories come with you. Everyone's the same color today.
screen: `THE THIRD EYE OPENS.` · `ANANGA, LOVE WITHOUT A BODY.` · `TWO FIRES, THEN THE COLORS.` · `SEVENTY-FIVE DAYS OF STORIES.` · then, large: `EVERYONE'S THE SAME COLOR TODAY.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: let go of one small grudge, and let it turn into something else. Sit, and breathe. Bring the grudge to mind. Picture it as Kama's arrow, sharp and pointed at you. Now picture it burning to ash. Then, instead of nothing, let something bodiless take its place: a little goodwill toward that person, invisible, but real. Breathe that in. Let it spread. The bell holds the time.
Holi. The festival of colors, the morning after the fire, where Prahlad, Radha and Kama all have a story.
Your line: everyone's the same color today. Today, look back over the stories, pick the one person from them you'd want beside you, and say why, out loud. Day ninety-six.

screen: `DAY 96 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE BREATH YOU ALREADY HAVE.`

howItsDone: In parts of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, the Holi full moon is kept as Kama Dahanam, remembering Kama burned by Shiva's third eye, with bonfires and songs; across India, the day after the full moon is kept with colors.

fork.setup: you're Shiva, deep in meditation. suddenly a flower arrow strikes your heart. what do you do?
options: go and find who shot it.
fork.reveal: his third eye opens and Kama burns to ash. then, moved by Rati's grief, Shiva lets love live on without a body.

original.note: Sanskrit: without a body, a name for Kama after Shiva's fire.

trapdoor: what you thought: Holi is just colors.
what it means: three Holi stories: Prahlad in the fire, Kama burned into a love that's everywhere, and Krishna and Radha's colors the morning after.
what a scholar hears: the burning of Kama is told in Kalidasa's Kumarasambhava and in the Puranas; Kama Dahanam at Holi is a southern regional custom.

notes: Kama's burning: Shiva Purana (Rudra Samhita) and Kumarasambhava 3 (Rati's lament in canto 4). The promise that Kama lives on bodiless (Ananga), and later reborn as Pradyumna in some tellings. Confirm.
Kama Dahanam at Holi in parts of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka: confirm regions.
